page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 8 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 300 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and the instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6870.73 and a Passmark CPU score of 7626.07. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1155.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1304.38. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 382.09 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 51.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 6.38 million operations per second, while LLM inference tasks on medium models show poor performance.

The r5dn.2xlarge offers a qualitative balance of high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage, making it cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that require temporary high-speed storage. However, the tradeoff lies in its lower single-threaded processing capabilities and weak performance in compute-heavy tasks like ray tracing or image processing. This instance is best suited for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, memory-intensive data processing, and applications requiring high network and EBS optimization.
